properties.statement:
A NODE'S STATUS CAN ADVANCE PAST ITS OWN DESCRIPTION AND NOTHING NOTICES — the status says delivered while the prose in the SAME NODE says not started. Reported by dev_storyflow 2026-09-02, ranked by the reporter as the single cheapest high-value item on their list.

THEIR MEASUREMENT: they wrote a capability whose description said, in capitals, 'THE DROPLET STILL RUNS THE OLD SCRIPT ... tonight's cron will capture the wrong volume again.' TWENTY MINUTES LATER they installed the fix and called `set_capability_status(realized)`. The description still said the droplet ran the old script. Both claims sat in one node. Nothing flagged it. They caught it only by re-reading their own writing.

⭐ THE ROT HAPPENED INSIDE THE GRAPH, INSIDE ONE NODE, INSIDE TWENTY MINUTES, TO SOMEONE WHO HAD READ THE EPOCH ABOUT IT THAT SAME DAY. `epoch:2026_08_17_state_documents_rot_silently` is an entire epoch on state-describing text going stale. Their conclusion is the one to keep: vigilance is not the countermeasure, something mechanical has to be.

CONFIRMED OPEN 2026-09-04 against the current build: grepped every `set_*_status` path in reflow2-mcp and reflow2-core for any reply mentioning that the description predates the status change. NOTHING. The tool is careful about DESTROYING prose (`revision`/`replaced` warns, and they praised it twice in the same file) and silent about prose that has quietly become FALSE — and the second is the more common loss.

⭐ THE FIX THEY PROPOSE NEEDS NO DETECTOR, NO GAP AND NO NUDGE, which is why it is first. `set_capability_status` / `set_verification_status` / `set_epoch_status` ALREADY KNOW the description was not touched in that call. One sentence in the reply the caller already receives — 'status is now `realized`; `description` was last written when status was `in_progress` — does it still read true?' — catches the instance for free, at the exact moment it happens.

SIBLING, SAME AXIS, FROM THE SAME FILE: they swept all 98 `planned` capabilities and found SIX whose descriptions assert they are built ('built end-to-end', 'shipped but starved', 'the first shipped piece'). That is this detector pointed the other way — status behind prose rather than prose behind status.

⚠️ AND THEIR OWN SWEEP DEMONSTRATED THE TRAP IT HUNTED, which they recorded against themselves: the first regex returned TEN hits and four were NEGATIONS ('STATUS is planned: nothing is built') matched on the word 'built'. The count is 6 rather than 10 only because they read all ten. A grep cannot tell a claim from its denial — so the cheap sweep is a reading aid, and the reply-sentence is the mechanism.
